correctness.rationale: Degree-one b1 and an force the universal adjacent endpoints a1,bn positive. With those both positive, every positive vertex has a positive neighbor; all remaining restrictions are zero-neighborhood sums. Split endpoints (2,2),(2,1),(1,2),(1,1). Cases with a 2 endpoint have a unique farthest positive index threshold; case (1,1) has unique first positive a at L and last positive b at R with exactly L≤R+1 and an explicit gap count. These disjoint exhaustive choices yield the three polynomial sums and rational size-generating series by geometric convolution. Setting z=1 gives the closed total and its limit; terms of degree4 give four minimizers at n=2 and exactly one at n≥3. Independently enumerated all 3^(2n) ternary labelings directly against neighborhood definitions n=2..5 and compared every coefficient to the formula: totals 25,209,1825,16265. Arbitrary n follows threshold bijections, not finite data.
residual_risks: Independent finite tests cannot alone prove infinite quantified claims; analytic premises and structural lemmas reconstructed.
